statements.venue: Campaign press release releasing his 'Making AI Work for Mississippi' plan
statements.quote: That is why I am calling for an immediate pause on data center construction until tech companies sign commitments that they will pay their fair share, including ensuring jobs are not temporary and paying for the energy that these data centers require without jacking up our utility bills.
statements.context: Announcing his plan for data centers in Mississippi, focused on power bills, water, local jobs and local control, and criticising Hyde-Smith's backing by an AI industry super PAC.
statements.source_label: Scott Colom for Senate press release
statements.reason: The pause he calls for is on data center construction for cost and jobs reasons; no catastrophic risk from AI is acknowledged.

statements.context: One of five rules in his plan, headed 'If AI touches our lives, a real person must answer for it', which also covers AI scams and fake images.
statements.source_label: Scott Colom for Senate campaign website
statements.reason: Human accountability for automated decisions about money, health care and benefits, plus scams and fake images, is outside catastrophic AI risk.

notes: Ten web searches ran, all listed in 'searches'; none were refused; the required searches on superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium, China agreement, 'AI safety' and a site-restricted search of scottcolom.com all ran. The site-restricted search returned no pages from his site, so I opened his site's pages directly instead. He was not a senator in September 2026, so he could not have signed the 23 September 2026 letter on AI talks with China (he is not on the verified signer list) or co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act; I found no source showing he commented on either. The three quotes were checked character for character against the raw page HTML of his campaign site (saved and parsed, not via a summarising tool). Quotes 2 and 3 are campaign plan text in the third person rather than words he spoke; the first-person quote in the press release is attributed to him. Left out: (1) Ecoportal (Spanish, 5 Oct 2026) gives his words only in Spanish translation, e.g. that data centers 'pueden aumentar los costos y ejercer presión sobre nuestra red eléctrica, el agua y la infraestructura'; translations are not his exact words, and the content is level D anyway. (2) The 26 Sep 2026 press release asking Hyde-Smith to reject AI super PAC money (level D; read only through a summarising tool). (3) WLOX, 23 Oct 2026: the state attorney general asked his campaign to remove AI-generated ads as possible political deepfakes; Colom called the video 'parody' and deleted it; no view on AI risk. Mississippi Today articles of 24 Sep and 13 Oct 2026 could not be opened (HTTP 403). An AI pact signed by about 18 candidates in August 2026 (mandatory safety reviews of AI models) was found, but the page I opened names only Dan Osborn; I could not tell whether Colom signed. Caution: a site called colomforsenate.com was built by Hyde-Smith's campaign to imitate him (Mississippi Today, per search summary); his real site is scottcolom.com. No debate transcript was checked.
